title: Windows 10 End of Life: Linux & Zorin OS Surge | Windows 11 AI Future
text:
Windows 10 Users Flock to Linux as Microsoft Support Ends
As Microsoft officially ended support for Windows 10 on October 14, a growing number of users are exploring alternatives, with Linux distributions seeing a significant surge in adoption.Reports indicate approximately 400 million PCs are now unsupported,leaving users to consider upgrading to Windows 11,purchasing extended support,continuing to use the OS at thier own risk,or abandoning the Microsoft ecosystem altogether.
The Exodus from Windows
While still early days, the shift away from Windows is becoming increasingly apparent. A recent report suggests a substantial number of users are choosing to migrate to Linux, driven by concerns over security, privacy, and the increasing costs associated with remaining within the Microsoft ecosystem.
Zorin OS Sees Explosive Growth
Leading the charge is Zorin OS, a Linux-based operating system specifically designed to be a seamless transition for Windows and macOS users. According to reports from Tom’s Hardware, Zorin OS 18 recently surpassed one million downloads following its latest update. “We’re thrilled to announce that Zorin OS 18 has amassed 1 million downloads in just over a month since its release, breaking all previous records,” a company release stated.
Perhaps even more telling, the developers claim that 78% of these downloads originated from Windows devices. While this figure doesn’t definitively mean all were direct migrations from Windows 10, it signals a strong interest from the Windows user base.
Beyond Curiosity: Performance and Privacy Drive Adoption
According to TechRadar, the surge in Zorin OS downloads is likely fueled by a combination of factors. Some users may simply be testing the platform,but the operating system’s ability to run efficiently on older hardware is a major draw,particularly as the debate over planned obsolescence intensifies following Microsoft’s decision to end support for Windows 10.
Zorin OS also offers enhanced privacy features and a user interface that closely resembles the familiar Windows habitat, easing the transition for newcomers.
The “end of 10” Campaign Gains Momentum
The movement to leave Windows isn’t solely organic. A grassroots group calling itself end of 10 has actively campaigned for Windows 10 users to switch to Linux, emphasizing the benefits of an ad-free and telemetry-free operating system. The campaign specifically targets users with older devices, positioning Linux as a viable choice to costly upgrades or risky unsupported usage.
Microsoft’s AI Push Faces Resistance
This user migration comes on the heels of Microsoft’s announcement to evolve Windows into an “agentic AI OS,” a decision that was met with considerable backlash from some users.The shift in focus towards artificial intelligence appears to have alienated a segment of the user base.
Why did users start migrating? Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 on October 14, leaving approximately 400 million PCs vulnerable. Concerns about security, privacy, cost, and Microsoft’s focus on AI also fueled the shift.
Who is leading the migration? Zorin OS is experiencing explosive growth,with 78% of its recent downloads originating from Windows devices. The “End of 10” grassroots campaign is also actively encouraging users to switch.
What is happening?
